title: Void Ending in a Square to Mercury
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Mercury, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his quicksilver turn of mind. Mercury is intellect's planet: learning, dialectic, geometry, astronomy, writing, and the reading of tongues, with every craft found by subtle talent under his governance. He rules the tongue, the brain, and the sensory memory, and quicksilver among the metals. The electional doctrine guards him closely: a work founded on Mercury must not find him retrograde, burning in the Sun's beams, or under an unfortunate planet's gaze.
